corrections.finding: 'near empty' is stronger than the source's 'relatively empty'.
corrections.fixed_text: Ants of Temnothorax albipennis moving house: a recruiter leads one follower at a time to a new site in a tandem run while the site is relatively empty, and as enough nestmates are there, recruiters switch to carrying the colony's passive majority, at a rate three times a tandem run's, tandem runs going on now and then in the other direction, back toward the old nest. A quorum at a new site is a colony's moment of parity changing from now-existing at its old nest to next-existing at its new one, and the runs back are podaling, away and back, across and along.

corrections.finding: 'about each other day' is unclear (reads as 'each other'); source says raids about every other day, and 'every' is a dissolved word.
corrections.fixed_text: An army ant colony, Eciton burchellii, goes in two phases with its brood: some twenty days at one bivouac, a living nest of its own hanging workers, as its pupae and new eggs develop, raiding on about alternate days; and as its eggs hatch and its pupae open, some fifteen days nomadic, raiding each day and moving its bivouac, mostly by night, six to eight hours a move. A colony stable-forms at one place as its brood develops, and as its brood opens, its next arriving within it, it is-not stable-forming at one place and goes on, a social abundancing moving it.

corrections.finding: 'gone' is a dead word (past participle); source says 4-6 hours after food removal.
corrections.fixed_text: Amoebae of the cellular slime mould Dictyostelium discoideum live as single cells, and some 4 to 6 hours after they have no food, up to 100,000 of them move in toward a centre along waves of cAMP each cell passes on to the next, and their gathering goes on as one slug, its tip leading, turning toward light and moving some 50 percent faster with it. Single cells are-not stable-forming where food is-not, and a society opens as one self going, toward a light over its surface.

corrections.finding: 'blocking serotonin' is stronger/unclear: source blocks serotonin receptors or production, not serotonin; 'serotonin alone' is unclear: source is injected serotonin with no other locusts present.
corrections.fixed_text: A desert locust lives in a solitary form or a gregarious form, both in one genome; crowding on shrinking patches of plants brings the change, and in a laboratory some two hours of touching a solitary locust's hind legs, as a crowd's jostling does, brings it, its serotonin in its thorax rising about threefold for less than a day, blocking its serotonin receptors or its serotonin production preventing the change and injecting serotonin with no other locusts near bringing it; swarms go as billions over many square kilometres. A field's Jekyll and Hyde and a plague are its story over this: a locust in a crowd is-not stable-forming as solitary, and its genome's artifact has its next form ready, a society going.
